Chapter Eleven: The Chapter on Non-Attainment (Anuprāpti-varga). (1) Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
“If you eliminate one dharma, I shall certify that you have attained the state of an anāgāmin.”
What is this one dharma?
It is called sensual desire. O bhikṣus!
"When you have extinguished lustful desire, I shall testify that you have attained the stage of Anāgāmin.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this verse:
"Stained by lustful craving, sentient beings fall into the evil realms."
"One should diligently abandon craving and desire, and one will then become a non-returner (anāgāmin).
At that time, the bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
2. (II) Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
“When one dharma is extinguished, I declare that you have realized the state of *anāgāmin*.
What is this one dharma? It is namely: ill will.”
"O bhikṣus! You should extinguish hatred; I testify that you have attained the stage of Anāgāmin.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this verse:
"Stained by hatred, sentient beings fall into the evil realms;
one should diligently abandon hatred, and thus become a non-returner (*anāgāmin*).
At that time, the bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
3. Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"When one dharma is extinguished and one dharma is abandoned, I declare that you have realized the state of an Anāgāmin.
What is this one dharma? It is ignorance."
"Therefore, monks, you should extinguish ignorance; I shall bear witness for you all to the state of Anāgāmin.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this verse:
"Stained by ignorance, sentient beings fall into evil realms;
one should diligently abandon ignorance, and thus become a non-returner (anāgāmin).
At that time, the bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
4. Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"When one dharma is extinguished and one dharma is abandoned, I certify that you have attained the state of an Anāgāmin.
What is this one dharma?
It is stinginess and greed."
"Therefore, monks, you should extinguish stinginess and greed; I testify that you have attained the stage of Anāgāmin.
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke this verse:
"Stained by stinginess and greed, sentient beings fall into evil realms;
one should diligently abandon stinginess and greed, and thus become an Anāgāmin.
At that time, the bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
5 (Five) Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:

"Within this assembly, I have never seen a single phenomenon that cannot be subdued, nor one that is so ill-timed as to result in the experience of various painful retributions; that is to say, it is the mind."
"O bhikṣus! This mind is difficult to subdue, hard to find the right opportunity for, and it undergoes various painful retributions. Therefore, O bhikṣus!"
One should discern the mind; one should contemplate the mind; one should maintain wholesome mindfulness of all roots of goodness.
Thus, monks, you should train yourselves.
At that time, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, the bhikṣus rejoiced and practiced accordingly. (6) Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"In this assembly, I have never seen a single dharma that is so easy to subdue, so easily made timely, and so receptive to various wholesome rewards."
This is what is meant by "the mind.
Monks! You should discern the mind and cultivate wholesome thoughts regarding all roots of goodness.
"In this way, monks, you should train yourselves.
At that time, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, the monks rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
7 (Seven). Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"If there were anyone in this assembly who thought, 'I know them all,' that person would then be speaking falsely before this great assembly by not providing food and drink."
Furthermore, at another time, I may see this person giving rise to a mind of defiled attachment and thinking of wealth and goods, and then uttering a falsehood in the midst of the great assembly.

The reason for this, O bhikṣus, is that attachment to wealth and possessions is extremely difficult to relinquish; it causes people to fall into the three evil realms and prevents them from reaching the state of unconditioned liberation!
Therefore, monks! If such a thought has already arisen, you should abandon it;
if it has not yet arisen, do not give rise to it again, nor allow your minds to become stained by attachment to material wealth.
"In this way, monks, you should train yourselves.
At that time, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, the monks rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
(8) Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, Anāthapiṇḍada’s Park.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"Within this assembly, one might think:
'Even at the cost of my life, I shall not utter a falsehood within this assembly.
Yet, at another time, I may observe this person and, giving rise to a mind of attachment and thinking of wealth, I then utter a falsehood within the great assembly."

The reason for this, O bhikṣus, is that attachment to wealth and possessions is extremely difficult to relinquish; it causes people to fall into the three evil realms and prevents them from reaching the state of unconditioned tranquility.
Therefore, monks, having already given rise to such a mind, you should abandon it;
if it has not yet arisen, do not give rise to it again with a mind stained by attachment to material wealth.
"In this way, monks, you should train yourselves.
At that time, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, the monks rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
9. Thus have I heard: At one time, the Buddha was staying at Rājagṛha in the Kalandaka Bamboo Grove, together with a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the bhikṣus:
"What do you think, bhikṣus?
Is there anyone who sees any pure dharma in Devadatta?"
Furthermore, Devadatta’s evil is so profound and grave that he shall undergo retribution for kalpas and cannot be healed.
Within my Dharma, not even a hair’s breadth of goodness is found in him that could be praised or recorded.
For this reason, I now declare that the source of Devadatta’s various transgressions is incurable.
It is just as if someone were to fall into a deep latrine, their body submerged and sinking so that there is not a single clean spot remaining.

Suppose there were someone who wished to rescue their life and place them in a clean location; they would thoroughly examine the area around the latrine and the person's body to see if there were any spot that was clean, thinking, "I wish to grasp them with my hand and pull them out to save them."
That man scrutinized it closely, but finding not a single clean spot that could be grasped, he abandoned it and departed.
In this same way, monks!
I observe that the foolish person Devadatta did not see even a hair’s breadth of a dharma worth upholding; he shall undergo retribution for kalpas, beyond all remedy.

The reason for this is that Devadatta was foolish and single-mindedly intent on his pursuit; being biased toward gain and offerings, he committed the five heinous crimes and, upon the dissolution of the body at the end of life, was reborn in the evil realms.
Thus it is, monks! Gain and offerings are profound and heavy; they prevent a person from reaching a state of peace and security. Therefore, monks!
If the thought of seeking gain and offerings has arisen, you should immediately abandon it;
if it has not yet arisen, do not give rise to such defiled thoughts. Thus, O bhikṣus!
"You should train yourselves in this way.
At that time, the bhikṣus, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly. 10 (10) Thus have I heard:
At one time, the Buddha was staying at the Kalandaka Bamboo Grove in Rājagṛha together with a great assembly of five hundred bhikṣus.
At that time, there was a certain bhikṣu who heard the Tathāgata’s prediction regarding Devadatta, that he would undergo punishment for one kalpa and could not be cured.
Then, that bhikṣu went to where the Venerable Ānanda was, and after exchanging greetings with him, sat down to one side.
At that time, the bhikṣu asked Ānanda: "How is it, Ānanda?"
The Tathāgata has fully observed the original nature of Devadatta; he then made this prediction: that he shall suffer punishment for one kalpa and cannot be cured.
Is there perhaps some underlying cause by which such a prediction could be made?
At that time, Ānanda said:
"What the Tathāgata has spoken can never be in vain; there is no discrepancy between his words and his deeds.
The Tathāgata has truly prophesied that Devadatta shall undergo profound and heavy retribution, which he must endure for an entire kalpa and cannot be cured."
At that time, the Venerable Ānanda rose from his seat, went to where the Blessed One was, prostrated with his head at the Blessed One’s feet, and stood to one side.
Then, Ānanda addressed the Blessed One, saying:
“A certain bhikṣu came to me and spoke as follows:”
"How is it, Ānanda? Having fully observed the original roots of Devadatta, does the Tathāgata then declare that he shall suffer punishment for one kalpa and cannot be cured?"
"Is there any cause or condition by which a prediction [of future enlightenment] may be granted?
Having spoken these words, they each departed.
The World-Honored One said:
"That bhikṣu must have entered the monastic life late in his studies; it has not been long since he first came to my Dharma.
What the Tathāgata speaks is never false; why, then, do you give rise to doubt regarding this?"
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed Ānanda, saying:
"Go to him and say to the bhikṣu:
'The Tathāgata summons you.'"
Ānanda replied, “So it is, World-Honored One!”
At that time, Ānanda, having received the instruction of the World-Honored One, went to where that bhikṣu was; having arrived, he said to that bhikṣu, "The Tathāgata summons you."
That bhikkhu replied: "So it is,
Venerable Sir!"
Then, that bhikṣu adjusted his robes and, together with Ānanda, went to where the Blessed One was.
Having arrived, he prostrated at the feet of the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed those bhikṣus:
"How is this, foolish men!
Do you not believe what the Tathāgata has spoken?"
"What the Tathāgata teaches is without falsehood; yet you now wish to seek falsehood in the Tathāgata.
Then that bhikṣu addressed the World-Honored One, saying, "The bhikṣu Devadatta possesses great supernormal power and great majestic authority."
"Why did the World-Honored One declare that he would suffer heavy retribution for one kalpa?
The Buddha told the bhikṣu:
"Guard your speech; do not undergo immeasurable suffering throughout the long night."
At that time, the World-Honored One spoke these verses:
"Practicing dhyāna with worldly supernormal powers, One ultimately attains no liberation;
Failing to create the track of cessation, One falls back again into hell."
"If I had seen even a hair’s breadth of wholesome dharma in Devadatta, I would never have declared that Devadatta would suffer punishment for one kalpa, incurable."
Therefore, you foolish man!
I do not see even a hair’s breadth of wholesome dharma in Devadatta; for this reason, I have declared that Devadatta shall suffer punishment for one kalpa and cannot be cured.

The reason for this is that Devadatta was foolish and deluded; greedily attached to gain and offerings, he gave rise to a mind of defiled attachment and committed the five heinous crimes. When his body perished and his life ended, he fell into hell.
The reason for this is that a mind heavy with gain and honor destroys the roots of goodness in people and prevents them from reaching a state of peace and security! Therefore, O bhikṣus!
If a mind of gain and sustenance arises, you should seek its cessation;
if no such mind exists, do not give rise to thoughts of attachment.
Thus it is, O bhikṣus!
"One should train in this way.
At that time, the bhikṣu rose from his seat, adjusted his robes, prostrated at the feet of the World-Honored One, and said to him:
"I now repent my transgression; I only pray that you will grant me your forgiveness!"
"Due to my ignorance, I have committed unwholesome deeds.
What the Tathāgata has spoken is without contradiction; yet, out of my own folly, I gave rise to thoughts of doubt."
"I only pray that the World-Honored One will accept my repentance, that I may reform my past ways and cultivate myself for the future.
This he repeated a second and a third time.
The World-Honored One said to him:
“Excellent, bhikṣu! Regret what you have thought;
forgive your lack of understanding, and do not harbor thoughts of doubt regarding the Tathāgata.”
"I now accept your confession; do not commit it again in the future.
This was repeated three or four times.
At that moment, the World-Honored One spoke this verse:
"Even if one has committed a grave offense, if they repent and do not commit it again,
this person should be restrained by the precepts, for the root-source of their transgression has been uprooted.
At that time, those bhikṣus and the fourfold assembly, having heard what the Buddha had spoken, rejoiced and practiced accordingly.
